data.why: The real WHO FluNet export (data/raw/VIW_FNT.csv) is git-ignored and not bundled, so a 160-week synthetic country-week series for Bangladesh (BGD) was written matching the exact VIW_FNT column schema used by src/pathogenwatch/io.py and cleaning.py, including deliberate data-quality cases (a zero-specimen week, a week where INF_ALL must be recovered from INF_A+INF_B, a week split across SENTINEL/NONSENTINEL source rows, an exact duplicate row, a missing calendar week, and an unseasonal spike week) so every dashboard tab has something real to show.

goals: Audit the raw WHO FluNet export for duplicates, missingness, source-combination conflicts, and internal consistency before trusting any downstream estimate
Review weekly and annual influenza positivity with 95% confidence intervals and specimen denominators to gauge current activity
Inspect the seasonal decomposition (robust STL and a harmonic quasi-binomial model) to characterize the recurring epidemic calendar and test for a month effect
Screen the positivity series for unusual weeks using EARS C1/C2/C3 and seasonal-baseline CUSUM detectors, and judge how many alerts are plausible outbreak signals versus noise
Compare one-week-ahead forecast performance of a simple last-week baseline against a Random Forest model on a chronological holdout, and decide whether the added complexity is justified
Switch country/area and year-range filters to check how coverage and interpretability change for other locations

review.summary: The tree follows the README's stated workflow closely: audit, summarise with uncertainty, seasonality, screening and judging alerts, a forecast against a baseline, and switching scope. The labels are clean, and 10 of the 11 screens checked match what their nodes say. One evidence citation is wrong, and the forecast phase leaves out the seasonal-naive baseline and doesn't say that the synthetic data reverses the README's forecast result, so it needs small fixes before filing.
